reason: The carrier needs to be ready for the two cores, and this is the only offered action.
expectation: I expect to place or prepare the carrier at the cold transfer bench, though I don't know exactly how the transfer will work.

effect: The carrier and its buffer are now chilled, with room for both whole cores. I can start loading them.
reaction: The space for surrounding ice reinforces why the cores were kept intact.
reason: The stored source core needs to go into the carrier, and this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the source core to be fitted into one cradle while remaining sealed and cold.

effect: The source core is in the carrier's first compartment, leaving the second ready for the band core.
reaction: It's reassuring that each core has its own compartment.
reason: The band core also needs to travel in the carrier, and this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the band core to be transferred into the second compartment while its liner and surrounding ice remain intact and cold.

effect: Both cores are now in separate cradles, ready for transfer to flight cooling.
reaction: Seeing the folded outline still visible in its liner is satisfying.
reason: The packed cores need flight cooling, and this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the carrier to connect to the lander's refrigerated sample bay, keeping both cores cold for flight.

effect: The carrier is secured to the lander's powered cooling, completing the transfer of both cores.
reaction: The buffer bridging the transfer was a reassuring detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: Chilling the carrier was worthwhile because its buffer and whole-core cradles made the cold transfer understandable.

leastWorthwhile.text: Loading the two cores felt repetitive because each was the only offered combination, though their separate compartments had a clear purpose.

surprise.text: I learned that the carrier's thermal buffer bridges the transfer before the lander's refrigerator takes over.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although the single available combination at each step left no meaningful choice.

continue.text: I would continue to learn what the receiving lab finds in the cores; their preserved surroundings make that question interesting.
